Increase in Parking Demand With Start of PD Building Construction

Construction on the new Broomfield Police Building project began in late July and will continue for approximately 20 months. During this time, parking availability for Police Department employees will be significantly reduced due to construction activity, fleet parking needs and site safety requirements.

As a result, there will be an increase in parking demand in the lots in front of and adjacent to the current Police Department headquarters, the Municipal Courts and the George Di Ciero City and County Building. Please plan appropriately if you are coming to these buildings to do business with the county, the police department or have a court date.

The aerial view map of the parking lot of the City and County of Broomfield complex shows that the parking lot behind the current Police Department building will be closed, the spaces toward the front of all lots are for visitor parking and the back lots are shown as employee parking.

Project Progress Timelapse

Watch the Police Expansion Project take shape over time through our project timelapse video. This visual timeline provides a unique look at the construction progress and the transformation of the project site from start to finish.

Project Background:

The Broomfield Police Department is headquartered at 7 DesCombes Drive where it occupies half the building (35,424 SF).  The other half is occupied by Broomfield Combined Courts.  The existing facility is less than half the necessary size to accommodate current and anticipated operations. A new building is proposed immediately west of the current building, at the southeast corner of E. 3rd Avenue and DesCombes Drive where the solar panels are currently located.

Project Information:

The proposed building is approximately 83,000 SF, and is proposed to be located at the southeast corner of DesCombes Drive and 3rd Avenue.  The secure parking lot will be expanded, providing additional spaces for police fleet and personal vehicles. An additional vehicular gate will provide another entry/exit point onto Descombes Drive, allowing for quicker response times and redundancy in egress from the secure lot. A secure fence will be extended around the perimeter of the parking lot, providing additional physical and visual security for officers and staff. 

 Timeline:

  • A  public (neighborhood) meeting is scheduled for Wednesday, May 6th from 5-6:30 pm in the Elmwood 1 Conference Room at the Broomfield Community Center (280 Spader Way) .
  • Construction is anticipated to start in Summer 2026 and take approximately 20 months to complete.

Project Cost:

The project is anticipated to cost $81.6M. This includes design, construction and other owner’s costs such as water and sewer licenses, tap fees, furniture, equipment, utility relocations including the solar panels, cable TV, and moving costs.
